name: Santa Cruz Itundujia Mixtec
confidence_why: No description of stress in Itundujia Mixtec exists; the only statement that covers the variety is Josserand's 1983 family-wide claim that the Mixtec couplet carries stress on its first syllable, known here only as quoted by Carroll 2015 and by Penner 2019 (who takes it as a Proto-Mixtec reconstruction), while Josserand's own Itundujia material is a 188-item wordlist with no stress or tone marking.

catalog_quote: Generalizing across Mixtec varieties, Josserand (1983:180) defines the couplet as “composed of two syllables and carrying stress on the first of these two,” implying that all Mixtec varieties have the same stress behavior. Besides the data from Santo Domingo Nuxaa shown in (4.2), several other descriptions support the characterization of stress in Mixtec as falling on the first vowel of the couplet. [...] In sum, default stress on the first syllable of the couplet is widely reported in Mixtec. [Carroll 2015:86-87] || Table A.2 (p. 276): Santa Cruz Itundujia Itu Itun mce Alta:W || The facts of IM word stress described here concord with the general state of affairs in Mixtec. Stress on the penultimate syllable or vowel of the couplet (or similar structure with a different descriptive label) is reported in the vast majority of Mixtec descriptions (e.g. ... Nuyoo Mixtec, Harris & Harris 2006:2), and Josserand 1983:180 posits stress on the penult syllable of the couplet for Proto-Mixtec. [Penner 2019:91-92]

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Quote: both segments of the reported quote are verbatim in, lines 5440-5443 ('Generalizing across Mixtec varieties, Josserand (1983:180) defines the couplet as "composed of two syllables and carrying stress on the first of these two," implying that all Mixtec varieties have the same stress behavior.') and lines 5490-5491 ('In sum, default stress on the first syllable of the couplet is widely reported in Mixtec.'); extracted text of the PDF confirms this is PDF page 108 = printed p. 86, section 4.2.1, exactly as the locator says (the '[..]' is the compiler elision of the intervening per-variety survey: Ayutla, Jicaltepec, Acatlan, Diuxi, Mixtepec, Atatlahuca, Silacayoapan, Alacatlatzala -- n…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Pan-Mixtec generalization (Josserand's dialect survey, which includes Santa Cruz Itundujia among its 122 towns): the root/stem 'couplet' is disyllabic (bimoraic) and stress falls on its first syllable, i.e. the penultimate syllable of the couplet; no Itundujia-specific stress description exists.
new_statements.exceptions: None for Itundujia. Carroll notes (pp. 86-87) that in some varieties (Silacayoapan, Alacatlatzala, Atatlahuca) vocalic enclitics shift the computation, and that Yoloxochitl Mixtec has been described with final stress -- none of this concerns Itundujia.
new_statements.domain_note: Domain is the lexical couplet (disyllabic/bimoraic root or stem), not the phonological word with clitics/prefixes; statement is a survey-wide generalization by Josserand, reported second-hand by Carroll. Itundujia's own data in circulation is only Josserand's 188-item wordlist, untonemarked and without stress marks.
new_statements.identity_note: No source describes Itundujia Mixtec (itun1239, mce) itself. The only stress statement whose scope covers it is Josserand's (1983:180) survey-wide generalization over all Mixtec varieties (Santa Cruz Itundujia = Josserand town code 'Itun', Carroll 2015 Table A.2, group Alta:W; Auderset et al. subgroup 6.2.2 Western Alta; Glottolog Chalcatongic). The variety is reported moribund (Julián Caballero 2009 lists Itundujia among communities that no longer speak Mixtec), which is consistent with the total absence of dedicated documentation.

new_statements.relation_note: Same placement and type as the record held by the project (Josserand 1983:180 via Carroll 2015: stress on the first syllable of the couplet = penultimate): Macaulay's endnote says 'in many of the dialects, stress is penultimate.. coincides with the first syllable [of the couplet]'. It is a pan-Mixtec generalization inside a grammar of Chalcatongo Mixtec (sanm1296, San Miguel el Grande Mixtec [mig]), a Chalcatongic sister of Itundujia; Itundujia is not named in any snippet, so it adds no Itundujia-specific evidence. Snippet-only; unchanged from the compilers' finding.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Cross-dialect remark: in many Mixtec dialects stress is penultimate, i.e. on the first syllable of the (bisyllabic) couplet; some dialects (e.g. Alacatlazala) have final stress in certain contexts. Nothing specific to Itundujia is visible in the snippets.
new_statements.exceptions: dialects without consistent penultimate stress exist; Alacatlazala (Zylstra 1980) has final stress in certain contexts (from snippets)
new_statements.identity_note: Macaulay 1996 describes Chalcatongo Mixtec (Chalcatongo de Hidalgo; Glottolog sanm1296, a dialect of San Miguel el Grande Mixtec [mig] sanm1295), a Chalcatongic (Western Alta) sister of Santa Cruz Itundujia Mixtec (itun1239); its stress endnote speaks of Mixtec dialects in general.
